contentObjective: I can find the greatest common factor (GCF) of two numbers by listing or comparing their factors.
languageObjective: I can explain how I found the GCF using the words factor, common factor, divisible, and greatest common factor.

noticeAndWonder.context: Mission Control has 24 food packs and 36 water containers to split into equal crew pods, with each pod getting the same number of each. Look at the factors of 24 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24) and the factors of 36 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36). What does each factor tell you about a possible number of pods, and which numbers appear in BOTH lists?

I notice 24 and 36 share ___ factors, and only the biggest one is the GCF because ___.

I wonder if prime factorization finds the GCF faster than listing every factor.
I wonder what the GCF would be if the numbers were ___ and ___ instead.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Party Favor Bags
revealWordProblem.text: Reginald is making party favor bags. He has 24 stickers and 36 erasers. He wants every bag to have the same number of stickers and the same number of erasers, with none left over, and he wants to make as many bags as possible. What is the greatest number of bags he can make, and how many stickers and erasers go in each bag? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The greatest number of bags is the GCF of 24 and 36. The common factors of 24 and 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12, so the GCF is 12. Reginald can make 12 bags, each with 24 ÷ 12 = 2 stickers and 36 ÷ 12 = 3 erasers, with none left over.

turnAndTalk.question: Mission Control must split 24 food packs and 36 water containers into equal crew pods, with each pod getting the same of each. Why won't the answer just be 24 or 36?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The number of pods must divide BOTH 24 and 36 evenly.

stems.en: The number of pods must be a factor of both ___ and ___.
stems.es: El número de cápsulas debe ser un factor de ___ y de ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students see the number of pods has to be a common factor of 24 and 36, so it must divide both with nothing left over, ruling out numbers that only divide one of them.
turnAndTalk.extend: If Mission Control added one more food pack (25 packs and 36 containers), how would that change the greatest number of equal pods? Justify your reasoning.

stems.en: The greatest common factor is ___ because ___.

extendStems: Using primes, 24 = ___ and 36 = ___, so the shared primes are ___.

turnAndTalk.question: A florist has 18 roses and 24 tulips and wants identical bouquets with no flowers left over. How does the GCF tell her the most bouquets she can make?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The GCF of 18 and 24 is the greatest number of equal bouquets.

stems.en: The florist can make ___ bouquets because the GCF of 18 and 24 is ___.

stems.en: Each bouquet gets ___ roses and ___ tulips.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute GCF(18, 24) = 6, so 6 bouquets, each with 3 roses and 4 tulips, and explain why a bigger number would leave flowers over.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why does the florist use the GREATEST common factor instead of just any common factor like 3? What changes if she picks a smaller one?
extendStems: She uses the greatest common factor because ___.
If she used 3 instead, she would make ___ bouquets, but ___.

turnAndTalk.question: How is the greatest common factor different from the least common multiple, and how can you tell which one a problem needs?
turnAndTalk.kernel: GCF splits things into equal groups; it is the largest shared factor.

stems.en: The GCF is the largest number that ___, but the LCM is the smallest number that ___.
stems.es: El MCD es el número más grande que ___, pero el mcm es el número más pequeño que ___.

stems.en: A problem needs the GCF when ___.
stems.es: Un problema necesita el MCD cuando ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students contrast GCF (largest factor that divides both, used to split into equal groups) with LCM (smallest shared multiple) and connect GCF to making equal groups with nothing left over.
turnAndTalk.extend: Two numbers are relatively prime (GCF = 1). What does that tell you about splitting them into equal groups? Give an example.
extendStems: If the GCF is 1, then the only equal grouping is ___ because ___.
An example is ___ and ___, which can only be split into ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Greatest Common Factor, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The GCF is the largest number that divides BOTH numbers with no remainder.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.NOS.4 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.

vocabulary.definition: The greatest whole number that divides two or more numbers with no remainder.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mayor número entero que divide dos o más números sin dejar residuo.
vocabulary.visual: Factors shared by 12 and 18 are 1, 2, 3, and 6, so GCF = 6.

sentences.text: The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 6.
The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 36.
The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 2.

vocabulary.definition: A factor of a whole number divides it evenly, with no remainder. For example, 3 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un factor de un número entero lo divide exactamente, sin dejar residuo. Por ejemplo, 3 es un factor de 12 porque 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
vocabulary.visual: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 — each divides 12 with no remainder
vocabulary.cloze: A number that divides evenly into another number with no remainder is a ___.

examples.why: 12 ÷ 5 leaves a remainder, so 5 is not a factor of 12.

vocabulary.definition: A number that divides two or more numbers evenly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que divide a dos o más números sin que sobre nada.
vocabulary.visual: 8 and 12 both divide evenly by 1, 2, and 4 — those are their common factors
vocabulary.cloze: A factor that two or more numbers share is a ___ factor.

vocabulary.definition: A number you can divide evenly, with nothing left over.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que se puede dividir sin que sobre nada.
vocabulary.visual: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 with no remainder, so 15 is divisible by 3
vocabulary.cloze: A number that can be divided by another with no remainder is ___ by that number.

vocabulary.definition: Writing a number as prime numbers multiplied together. It helps you find the GCF.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir un número como números primos multiplicados. Ayuda a encontrar el MCD.

conceptIntro.heading: What is the greatest common factor (GCF)?
conceptIntro.intro: A factor is a number that divides another number evenly, with nothing left over. The greatest common factor is the biggest factor that two numbers share.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: The GCF is the largest number that divides BOTH numbers with no remainder.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want the GCF of 24 and 36. First I list the factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24.
Next I list the factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36.
Now I circle the factors in BOTH lists: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. These are the common factors.
The biggest one is 12, so the GCF of 24 and 36 is 12. I check: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3. Both are even, so 12 works.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's find the GCF of 8 and 12. What are the factors of 8? (1, 2, 4, 8.)
What are the factors of 12? (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.) Which numbers are in both lists? (1, 2, 4.)
Which shared factor is the largest? (4.) So the GCF of 8 and 12 is 4.

Remember: pick the LARGEST factor the two numbers share.

discourse.prompt: What is the greatest common factor of 24 and 36? How did sorting the factors help you find it?

optional.stem: Mission Control must split 24 oxygen tanks and 36 ration packs into identical crew pods with none left over. What is the GCF of 24 and 36?
optional.explanation: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The greatest shared factor is 12, so 12 pods can be filled equally.
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
8 divides 24 evenly, but 36 ÷ 8 leaves a remainder. A common factor has to work for both numbers.
72 is a number that 24 and 36 both divide into, so it is a common multiple. A factor divides into the numbers instead.
optional.stemEs: El Control de Misión debe repartir 24 tanques de oxígeno y 36 paquetes de raciones en cápsulas idénticas para la tripulación, sin que sobre nada. ¿Cuál es el MCD de 24 y 36?
optional.explanationEs: Factores de 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factores de 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. El mayor factor compartido es 12, así que se pueden llenar 12 cápsulas por igual.
hints: The greatest common factor is the largest number that divides both amounts evenly, with nothing left over.
Write out every factor of 24 and every factor of 36, then look at which numbers show up on both lists.
Factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Start the list for 36 the same way — 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, ... — and find the largest number that appears on both lists.
hintsEs: El máximo común divisor es el número más grande que divide exactamente a las dos cantidades, sin que sobre nada.
Escribe todos los factores de 24 y todos los factores de 36, y luego observa qué números aparecen en las dos listas.
Los factores de 24 son 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Empieza la lista de 36 de la misma forma — 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, ... — y busca el número más grande que aparezca en las dos listas.

optional.stem: The astronaut crew has 40 solar cells and 60 battery cells to load into matching storage bins with nothing left over. What is the GCF of 40 and 60?
optional.explanation: Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. The greatest shared factor is 20, so 20 bins can be filled equally.
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
4 divides both 40 and 60, so it really is a common factor — but it is not the greatest one. Look further down your list for a bigger shared factor.
120 is a common multiple of 40 and 60, not a factor. A factor of 40 can never be larger than 40.
optional.stemEs: La tripulación de astronautas tiene 40 celdas solares y 60 celdas de batería para guardar en contenedores iguales sin que sobre nada. ¿Cuál es el MCD de 40 y 60?
optional.explanationEs: Factores de 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Factores de 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. El mayor factor compartido es 20, así que se pueden llenar 20 contenedores por igual.
hints: You need the largest number that divides both 40 and 60 evenly — that is what the greatest common factor means.
List the factors of the smaller number first. The GCF can never be larger than 40, so that list sets your ceiling.
Factors of 40 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Test them against 60 starting from the largest and stop at the first one that divides 60 with no remainder.
hintsEs: Necesitas el número más grande que divide exactamente a 40 y a 60: eso es el máximo común divisor.
Primero escribe los factores del número menor. El MCD nunca puede ser mayor que 40, así que esa lista marca el límite.
Los factores de 40 son 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Pruébalos con 60 empezando por el mayor y detente en el primero que divida a 60 sin residuo.

optional.label: Each crew pod needs the same number of each supply with none left over. Match each supply pair to the greatest number of equal pods (the GCF).
optional.explanation: Each pod must get the same number of tanks and the same number of packs with none left over, so the number of pods is the GCF of the two supply counts: GCF(18, 27) = 9, GCF(21, 28) = 7, GCF(32, 48) = 16, and GCF(25, 35) = 5.
optional.explanationEs: Cada cápsula debe recibir la misma cantidad de tanques y la misma cantidad de paquetes sin que sobre nada, así que el número de cápsulas es el MCD de las dos cantidades de suministros: GCF(18, 27) = 9, GCF(21, 28) = 7, GCF(32, 48) = 16 y GCF(25, 35) = 5.
hints: Splitting supplies into equal pods with nothing left over means the number of pods has to divide BOTH counts — that is a common factor.
For each card, list the factors of the smaller supply count, keep only the ones that also divide the larger count, then take the greatest.
Start with '18 tanks & 27 packs': the factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Test which of those also divide 27 evenly, then look for the largest.
hintsEs: Repartir los suministros en cápsulas iguales sin que sobre nada significa que el número de cápsulas tiene que dividir a LAS DOS cantidades: eso es un factor común.
Para cada tarjeta, lista los factores de la cantidad menor, quédate solo con los que también dividen a la cantidad mayor y luego toma el mayor de todos.
Empieza con '18 tanks & 27 packs': los factores de 18 son 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Prueba cuáles de esos también dividen a 27 exactamente y busca el más grande.
optional.labelEs: Cada cápsula de la tripulación necesita la misma cantidad de cada suministro, sin que sobre nada. Une cada pareja de suministros con la mayor cantidad de cápsulas iguales (el MCD).

optional.instructions: Mission Control is packing supply pairs into equal pods. Sort each pair by the largest number of equal pods it can fill (its GCF).
optional.explanation: 15 and 25 share a greatest common factor of 5, and so do 20 and 35, so both of those cards fill 5 equal pods. 30 and 42 share 6, and 18 and 24 also share 6, so those two cards fill 6 equal pods.
optional.explanationEs: 15 y 25 tienen un máximo común divisor de 5, y 20 y 35 también, así que esas dos tarjetas llenan 5 cápsulas iguales. 30 y 42 comparten 6, y 18 y 24 también comparten 6, así que esas dos tarjetas llenan 6 cápsulas iguales.
hints: The two labels already give you the answers: every card's GCF is either 5 or 6, so you just have to figure out which.
For each card, find the largest number that divides both supply counts evenly, then drop the card under the label that shows that number.
Take '15 tanks & 25 packs': the factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15. Check which of those also divide 25 evenly to find its pod count.
hintsEs: Las dos etiquetas ya te dan las respuestas: el MCD de cada tarjeta es 5 o 6, así que solo tienes que decidir cuál.
Para cada tarjeta, busca el número más grande que divide exactamente a las dos cantidades y colócala bajo la etiqueta que muestra ese número.
Toma '15 tanks & 25 packs': los factores de 15 son 1, 3, 5, 15. Revisa cuáles de esos también dividen exactamente a 25 para hallar su número de cápsulas.
optional.instructionsEs: Control de Misión está empacando parejas de suministros en cápsulas iguales. Clasifica cada pareja según la mayor cantidad de cápsulas iguales que puede llenar (su MCD).

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The Wrong Mission Number

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: Split 12 oxygen tanks and 18 ration packs into the most equal crew pods with none left over.

workedExample.label: Choose the number of pods
workedExample.work: Cadet Rio says 36 pods, because 36 is the smallest number that both 12 and 18 divide into.

optional.correctWork: Cadet Rio found the LCM (least common multiple = 36), but making equal groups with none left over needs the GCF (greatest common factor). The common factors of 12 and 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, and the greatest is 6. So Mission Control can fill 6 equal pods, each with 2 oxygen tanks and 3 ration packs.
hints: Splitting supplies INTO equal groups with none left over uses the GCF, not the LCM. The GCF is a factor that divides both numbers, so it must be 12 or smaller, not 36.
List the common factors of 12 and 18: 1, 2, 3, 6. Which one is the GREATEST? That is the number of pods.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: el número de misión equivocado
optional.explanation: Cadet Rio found 36, which is the least common multiple of 12 and 18, not the greatest common factor. Splitting supplies into equal groups with none left over needs a number that DIVIDES both counts, so it can never be bigger than 12. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, and 6, so Mission Control fills 6 pods with 12 ÷ 6 = 2 tanks and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 packs each.
optional.explanationEs: El cadete Rio encontró 36, que es el mínimo común múltiplo de 12 y 18, no el máximo común divisor. Repartir los suministros en grupos iguales sin que sobre nada necesita un número que DIVIDA a las dos cantidades, así que nunca puede ser mayor que 12. Los factores comunes son 1, 2, 3 y 6, así que Control de Misión llena 6 cápsulas con 12 ÷ 6 = 2 tanques y 18 ÷ 6 = 3 paquetes cada una.

approaching.stem: What is the GCF of 8 and 12?
approaching.explanation: Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The largest common factor is 4.
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
8 is a factor of 8, but check 12 ÷ 8 — it does not come out even. A common factor has to divide both numbers with nothing left over.
24 is a number that both 8 and 12 divide into, which makes it a common multiple, not a common factor. A factor is never larger than the number it belongs to.
hints: GCF means the GREATEST factor the numbers share. You need a number that divides BOTH 8 and 12, not just one of them.
List all the factors of 8, then all the factors of 12. Circle the numbers that appear in both lists and pick the largest.
Factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4, and 8. Now write out the factors of 12 and circle every number that shows up in both lists.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el máximo común divisor (MCD) de 8 y 12?
approaching.explanationEs: Factores de 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factores de 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. El mayor factor común es 4.
hintsEs: MCD significa el MAYOR factor que los números comparten. Necesitas un número que divida a AMBOS, 8 y 12, no solo a uno.
Escribe todos los factores de 8 y luego todos los de 12. Encierra los números que aparecen en ambas listas y elige el mayor.
Los factores de 8 son 1, 2, 4 y 8. Ahora escribe los factores de 12 y encierra cada número que aparezca en las dos listas.

approaching.stem: Which pair of numbers has a GCF of 5?
approaching.explanation: 15 = 3 × 5, 25 = 5 × 5. Both share the factor 5, and 5 is the largest shared factor.
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
This pair does share a factor, but test 5 against 6 first: 6 ÷ 5 leaves a remainder, so 5 cannot be a factor of both.
5 divides 20 evenly, so it is easy to stop here — but check 8 ÷ 5 too. Both numbers have to work.
hints: You're hunting for a pair where 5 divides BOTH numbers — and where no bigger number divides both.
Quick check: a number divisible by 5 ends in 0 or 5. After that test, confirm 5 is the LARGEST factor the pair shares.
Look at 10 and 12 first: 10 ends in 0, but does 5 divide 12 evenly? If not, that pair is out — test the other pairs the same way.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál pareja de números tiene un MCD de 5?
approaching.explanationEs: 15 = 3 × 5, 25 = 5 × 5. Los dos comparten el factor 5, y 5 es el mayor factor común.
hintsEs: Buscas una pareja en la que 5 divida a AMBOS números, y donde ningún número mayor divida a los dos.
Revisión rápida: un número divisible entre 5 termina en 0 o en 5. Después confirma que 5 sea el MAYOR factor que comparte la pareja.
Mira primero 10 y 12: el 10 termina en 0, pero ¿divide el 5 al 12 exacto? Si no, esa pareja queda fuera; prueba las demás igual.

approaching.stem: What is the GCF of 14 and 21?
approaching.explanation: Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factors of 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. The largest common factor is 7.
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
3 divides 21 evenly, but 14 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder. Test every candidate against both numbers before you choose.
1 divides every whole number, so it is always a common factor — but you are looking for the greatest one. Keep comparing the two factor lists.
hints: Both 14 and 21 appear in times tables you know. Which multiplication facts build each number?
Write each number as a multiplication fact, then compare: which factor shows up in both facts?
Factors of 14 are 1, 2, 7, and 14. Now list the factors of 21 and find the greatest number that lives in both lists.
approaching.explanationEs: Factores de 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factores de 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. El mayor factor común es 7.
hintsEs: Tanto 14 como 21 aparecen en tablas de multiplicar que ya conoces. ¿Qué multiplicaciones forman cada número?
Escribe cada número como una multiplicación y luego compara: ¿qué factor aparece en las dos?
Los factores de 14 son 1, 2, 7 y 14. Ahora escribe los factores de 21 y busca el mayor número que esté en ambas listas.

approaching.instructions: Sort these numbers: which are common factors of 16 and 20, and which are NOT?
hints: A common factor must divide 16 with no remainder AND divide 20 with no remainder. One miss means it's not common.
Test each card twice: divide 16 by the number, then divide 20 by it. Both divisions must come out even.
Try the card '8': 16 ÷ 8 = 2 works, but 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 does not — so 8 is NOT a common factor. Test each other card the same way.
approaching.explanation: The common factors of 16 and 20 are 1, 2, and 4, because each of those divides both numbers with no remainder. The cards 5, 8, and 10 each divide only one of the two numbers — 20 ÷ 5 = 4 but 16 ÷ 5 is not whole, and 16 ÷ 8 = 2 but 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 — so they are NOT common factors.
approaching.explanationEs: Los factores comunes de 16 y 20 son 1, 2 y 4, porque cada uno divide a los dos números sin dejar residuo. Las tarjetas 5, 8 y 10 dividen solo a uno de los dos números: 20 ÷ 5 = 4, pero 16 ÷ 5 no da un número entero, y 16 ÷ 8 = 2, pero 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5. Por eso NO son factores comunes.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica estos números: ¿cuáles son factores comunes de 16 y 20 y cuáles NO lo son?
hintsEs: Un factor común debe dividir a 16 sin residuo Y dividir a 20 sin residuo. Si falla en uno, no es común.
Prueba cada tarjeta dos veces: divide 16 entre el número y luego divide 20 entre él. Las dos divisiones deben ser exactas.
Prueba la tarjeta '8': 16 ÷ 8 = 2 funciona, pero 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 no, así que 8 NO es factor común. Prueba las demás igual.

approaching.stem: What is the GCF of 9 and 15?
approaching.explanation: Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. The largest common factor is 3.
choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
9 is a factor of 9, but 15 ÷ 9 leaves a remainder, so 9 is not shared by both numbers. Check each candidate against both.
45 is a number that 9 and 15 both divide into — that makes it a common multiple. Factors go the other direction: they divide into the numbers.
hints: Don't settle for 1 — most pairs share something bigger. What number multiplies into both 9 and 15?
List the factors of each number: 9 has just three factors and 15 has four, so the lists are short to compare.
Factors of 9 are 1, 3, and 9. Now write out the factors of 15 and pick the greatest number that appears in 9's list too.
approaching.explanationEs: Factores de 9: 1, 3, 9. Factores de 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. El mayor factor común es 3.
hintsEs: No te quedes con el 1: casi todas las parejas comparten algo mayor. ¿Qué número multiplica para formar 9 y también 15?
Escribe los factores de cada número: 9 tiene solo tres factores y 15 tiene cuatro, así que las listas son cortas de comparar.
Los factores de 9 son 1, 3 y 9. Ahora escribe los factores de 15 y elige el mayor número que también esté en la lista del 9.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake — Not the Greatest

workedExample.label: Choose the GCF
workedExample.work: Sam circles 3 and says the GCF of 12 and 30 is 3.

approaching.correctWork: The common factors of 12 and 30 are 1, 2, 3, and 6. Sam stopped at 3, but the GREATEST common factor is the largest one, which is 6. So GCF(12, 30) = 6.
hints: Sam listed the factors correctly. Look at the shared factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. Did Sam pick the largest one?
The GCF is the GREATEST common factor. The biggest number in the shared list 1, 2, 3, 6 is 6.
approaching.titleEs: Detecta el error común: no es el mayor
approaching.explanation: Sam's two factor lists are correct, and the factors that 12 and 30 share are 1, 2, 3, and 6. The mistake happens at the last step: 3 really is a common factor, but it is not the greatest one. The GCF is the largest number in the shared list, so GCF(12, 30) = 6.
approaching.explanationEs: Las dos listas de factores de Sam están correctas, y los factores que comparten 12 y 30 son 1, 2, 3 y 6. El error ocurre en el último paso: 3 sí es un factor común, pero no es el mayor. El máximo común divisor (MCD) es el número más grande de la lista compartida, así que GCF(12, 30) = 6.

onLevel.label: Match each pair of numbers to their GCF.
hints: Each match must divide BOTH numbers of its pair evenly. A quick divisibility check rules out bad matches fast.
For each pair, list the factors of the SMALLER number, then test which of those also divide the larger number.
Try GCF(6, 9): the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3, 6. Which of those divide 9 evenly? The biggest one that does is the match.
onLevel.explanation: Each match is the largest number that divides both numbers of its pair: GCF(6, 9) = 3, GCF(12, 18) = 6, GCF(16, 24) = 8, GCF(20, 30) = 10, GCF(15, 35) = 5, and GCF(14, 21) = 7. A quick way to check is to list the factors of the smaller number and keep the biggest one that also divides the larger number.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada emparejamiento es el número más grande que divide a los dos números de su par: GCF(6, 9) = 3, GCF(12, 18) = 6, GCF(16, 24) = 8, GCF(20, 30) = 10, GCF(15, 35) = 5 y GCF(14, 21) = 7. Una forma rápida de comprobarlo es listar los factores del número menor y quedarte con el mayor que también divide al número mayor.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada pareja de números con su MCD.
hintsEs: Cada pareja debe dividirse exacto entre AMBOS números. Una revisión rápida de divisibilidad descarta las malas parejas enseguida.
Para cada pareja, escribe los factores del número MENOR y luego prueba cuáles de ellos también dividen al mayor.
Prueba MCD(6, 9): los factores de 6 son 1, 2, 3 y 6. ¿Cuáles de esos dividen a 9 exacto? El mayor que lo haga es la respuesta.

onLevel.label: Use prime factorization to find the GCF.
hints: The prime factorizations are handed to you — your job is to spot which primes appear in BOTH factorizations.
Circle each prime that shows up in both lists (repeats only count as many times as BOTH have them), then multiply the circled primes.
Row 1: look at 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 and 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. Circle the primes both lists share, then multiply only what you circled.
onLevel.explanation: The GCF is the product of only the prime factors that appear in BOTH factorizations. 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 and 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 share 2 × 3 = 6; 30 and 45 share 3 × 5 = 15; 28 and 42 share 2 × 7 = 14. A repeated prime counts only as many times as both lists have it.
onLevel.explanationEs: El MCD es el producto de los factores primos que aparecen en LAS DOS factorizaciones. 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 y 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 comparten 2 × 3 = 6; 30 y 45 comparten 3 × 5 = 15; 28 y 42 comparten 2 × 7 = 14. Un factor primo repetido cuenta solo las veces que aparece en ambas listas.
onLevel.labelEs: Usa la factorización prima para encontrar el MCD.
hintsEs: Ya te dan las factorizaciones primas: tu trabajo es ver qué primos aparecen en AMBAS.
Encierra cada primo que aparezca en las dos listas (los repetidos cuentan solo las veces que están en AMBAS) y multiplica lo encerrado.
Fila 1: mira 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 y 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. Encierra los primos que comparten y luego multiplica solo lo que encerraste.

onLevel.stem: A teacher has 36 pencils and 48 erasers. She wants to make identical supply bags with no items left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
onLevel.explanation: GCF(36, 48) = 12. She can make 12 bags, each with 3 pencils and 4 erasers.
choiceFeedback: Is that really the biggest factor they share? Check your list again.
4 does divide both 36 and 48 evenly, so it is a common factor — it just is not the greatest one. Keep looking for a larger number that still divides both.
Are you sure that's the GREATEST? Check the smaller factors too.
hints: 'Identical bags with nothing left over' is the clue: the number of bags must divide 36 AND 48 with no remainder.
Find the greatest number that divides both 36 and 48 — list the common factors and take the largest one.
List the factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Now test which of these also divide 48 evenly, and take the greatest.
onLevel.stemEs: Una maestra tiene 36 lápices y 48 borradores. Quiere armar bolsas de materiales idénticas sin que sobre nada. ¿Cuál es la mayor cantidad de bolsas que puede armar?
onLevel.explanationEs: MCD(36, 48) = 12. Puede armar 12 bolsas, cada una con 3 lápices y 4 borradores.
hintsEs: 'Bolsas idénticas sin que sobre nada' es la pista: el número de bolsas debe dividir a 36 Y a 48 sin residuo.
Busca el mayor número que divida a 36 y a 48: escribe los factores comunes y toma el más grande.
Escribe los factores de 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Ahora prueba cuáles de ellos también dividen a 48 exacto y toma el mayor.

onLevel.instructions: Sort: which pairs have a GCF greater than 1, and which are relatively prime (GCF = 1)?
hints: Each card already tells you its GCF — read it closely. 'Relatively prime' simply means the GCF equals exactly 1.
Sort by the printed GCF: a GCF of exactly 1 goes to Relatively Prime; any GCF bigger than 1 goes to the other group.
Take '8 and 12 (GCF = 4)': 4 is greater than 1, so it belongs in the GCF Greater Than 1 group. Sort the rest by their printed GCF.
onLevel.explanation: Every card prints its own GCF, so the sorting rule is short: a GCF of exactly 1 means the two numbers share no factor besides 1, and that is what 'relatively prime' means — 7 and 11, 8 and 15, and 9 and 14. The cards with a GCF of 4, 3, and 5 all have a GCF greater than 1.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su propio MCD, así que la regla para clasificar es corta: un MCD de exactamente 1 significa que los dos números no comparten ningún factor además del 1, y eso es ser primos relativos: 7 y 11, 8 y 15, y 9 y 14. Las tarjetas con MCD de 4, 3 y 5 tienen un MCD mayor que 1.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica: ¿cuáles parejas tienen un MCD mayor que 1 y cuáles son primos entre sí (MCD = 1)?
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta ya dice su MCD; léela con cuidado. 'Primos relativos' simplemente significa que el MCD es exactamente 1.
Clasifica por el MCD impreso: un MCD de exactamente 1 va a Primos Relativos; cualquier MCD mayor que 1 va al otro grupo.
Toma '8 y 12 (MCD = 4)': 4 es mayor que 1, así que va al grupo MCD Mayor Que 1. Clasifica las demás por su MCD impreso.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake — GCF or LCM?

workedExample.label: Choose the answer
workedExample.work: Jordan multiplies 8 × 20 = 160 and says the GCF of 8 and 20 is 160.

onLevel.correctWork: Multiplying the two numbers does not give the GCF. The GCF is the largest factor the numbers SHARE. The common factors of 8 and 20 are 1, 2, and 4, so the GCF is 4 — and a factor can never be larger than the numbers themselves.
hints: A factor of 8 cannot be bigger than 8. Is 160 a factor of 8 and 20, or did Jordan multiply instead?
Find the common factors of 8 and 20: 1, 2, 4. The greatest one is 4, so GCF(8, 20) = 4.
onLevel.titleEs: Detecta el error común: ¿MCD o mcm?
onLevel.explanation: Jordan multiplied 8 × 20 to get 160, but multiplying two numbers produces a common multiple, not a common factor. A factor of 8 can never be larger than 8 itself. The factors 8 and 20 share are 1, 2, and 4, so GCF(8, 20) = 4.
onLevel.explanationEs: Jordan multiplicó 8 × 20 y obtuvo 160, pero multiplicar dos números produce un múltiplo común, no un factor común. Un factor de 8 nunca puede ser mayor que 8. Los factores que comparten 8 y 20 son 1, 2 y 4, así que GCF(8, 20) = 4.

extending.title: Find Amara's Mistake
extending.correctWork: GCF = 4 (the greatest of the common factors, not just any common factor). Amara found the common factors correctly but chose 2 instead of the largest one, 4.
hints: Amara found the common factors correctly. Look at Step 4 — did she pick the greatest one?
The GCF is the LARGEST common factor. Look at the list: 1, 2, 4. Which is biggest?
extending.explanation: Amara's factor lists and her list of common factors (1, 2, 4) are all correct. The error is in the last step: she chose 2, but the GCF has to be the greatest of the shared factors, which is 4. So the GCF of 16 and 28 is 4, not 2.
extending.explanationEs: Las listas de factores de Amara y su lista de factores comunes (1, 2, 4) están correctas. El error está en el último paso: eligió 2, pero el MCD tiene que ser el mayor de los factores compartidos, que es 4. Entonces el MCD de 16 y 28 es 4, no 2.

extending.prompt: A farmer has 54 apples and 36 oranges. She wants to make gift baskets where every basket has the same number of apples and the same number of oranges, with none left over. Find the greatest number of baskets and explain how you used GCF to solve this.
extending.sentenceFrame: The GCF of 54 and 36 is ___ because ___. So the farmer can make ___ baskets, each with ___ apples and ___ oranges.
hints: Re-read: every basket identical, nothing left over. The basket count must divide 54 AND 36 — and be the GREATEST number that does.
Find GCF(54, 36) using factor lists or prime factorization. Then divide 54 and 36 by that GCF to fill each basket.
Start: 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 and 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Multiply the primes both share to get the basket count, then divide to fill baskets.
extending.explanation: Every basket has to be identical with nothing left over, so the number of baskets must divide both 54 and 36 — and 'the greatest number of baskets' means the GCF. Since 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 and 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3, they share 2 × 3 × 3 = 18. The farmer makes 18 baskets, each with 54 ÷ 18 = 3 apples and 36 ÷ 18 = 2 oranges.
extending.explanationEs: Cada canasta debe ser igual y no puede sobrar nada, así que el número de canastas tiene que dividir a 54 y a 36, y 'la mayor cantidad de canastas' significa el MCD. Como 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 y 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3, comparten 2 × 3 × 3 = 18. La agricultora arma 18 canastas, cada una con 54 ÷ 18 = 3 manzanas y 36 ÷ 18 = 2 naranjas.
extending.promptEs: Una agricultora tiene 54 manzanas y 36 naranjas. Quiere armar canastas de regalo donde cada canasta tenga la misma cantidad de manzanas y la misma cantidad de naranjas, sin que sobre nada. Encuentra la mayor cantidad de canastas y explica cómo usaste el MCD para resolverlo.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer: cada canasta idéntica y sin que sobre nada. El número de canastas debe dividir a 54 Y a 36, y ser el MAYOR que lo hace.
Halla MCD(54, 36) con listas de factores o con factorización prima. Luego divide 54 y 36 entre ese MCD para llenar cada canasta.
Empieza: 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 y 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Multiplica los primos que comparten para hallar el número de canastas y luego divide.

extending.label: Find the GCF of each pair, then use it to simplify the fraction.
hints: The GCF column is your tool: dividing the top AND bottom by the GCF gives the simplest form in one step.
For each fraction, find the GCF of numerator and denominator first, then divide both parts by that same number.
For 12/18: list the factors of 12 and of 18, take the greatest one they share, then divide both 12 and 18 by it.
extending.explanation: Dividing the numerator and the denominator by their GCF gives the simplest form in one step: 12 and 18 divided by 6 give 2/3; 20 and 30 divided by 10 give 2/3; 24 and 36 divided by 12 give 2/3; 15 and 25 divided by 5 give 3/5. Using the GCF — not just any common factor — is what guarantees the fraction cannot be reduced again.
extending.explanationEs: Dividir el numerador y el denominador entre su MCD da la forma más simple en un solo paso: 12 y 18 entre 6 dan 2/3; 20 y 30 entre 10 dan 2/3; 24 y 36 entre 12 dan 2/3; 15 y 25 entre 5 dan 3/5. Usar el MCD, y no cualquier factor común, es lo que garantiza que la fracción ya no se pueda reducir más.
extending.labelEs: Encuentra el MCD de cada pareja y úsalo para simplificar la fracción.
hintsEs: La columna del MCD es tu herramienta: dividir el numerador Y el denominador entre el MCD da la forma simplificada en un solo paso.
Para cada fracción, halla primero el MCD del numerador y el denominador, y luego divide ambas partes entre ese mismo número.
Para 12/18: escribe los factores de 12 y los de 18, toma el mayor que comparten y luego divide 12 y 18 entre él.

optionalActivity.name: GCF Grouping Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Help Mission Control split the space station's supplies into the largest possible number of identical crew pods with nothing left over.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Greatest Common Factor is confusing it with the Least Common Multiple: some students list the MULTIPLES of both numbers and pick the smallest shared one (getting an answer bigger than either number, like 72 for 24 and 36) instead of listing FACTORS and picking the largest one they share (12). Remember: the GCF splits numbers INTO equal groups, so it can never be bigger than the smaller of the two numbers.

connect.scenario: A baker is making gift boxes with cookies and brownies. She has 48 cookies and 32 brownies. She wants every box to have the same number of cookies and the same number of brownies, with none left over.
connect.promptQuestion: How does the GCF help the baker? How many boxes can she make?
connect.prompt: The baker can make ___ boxes because the GCF of 48 and 32 is ___.

check.stem: What is the GCF of 48 and 32?
check.explanation: 48 = 2⁴ × 3 and 32 = 2⁵. The shared prime factors are 2⁴ = 16, so the GCF is 16. 8 divides both but it is not the greatest.

check.stem: How many cookies go in each box?
How many brownies go in each box?
check.explanation: 32 brownies ÷ 16 boxes = 2 brownies per box. Each box gets 3 cookies and 2 brownies with nothing left over.

connect.modelAnswer: The GCF of 48 and 32 is 16, so the baker can make 16 identical boxes. Each box gets 48 ÷ 16 = 3 cookies and 32 ÷ 16 = 2 brownies, with none left over. Any larger number of boxes would not divide both amounts evenly.

exitTicket.stem: What is the GCF of 18 and 27?
exitTicket.explanation: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. The factors they share are 1, 3, and 9, so the GCF is 9 — the GREATEST shared factor, not just any common factor (that rules out 3). Six divides 18 but not 27, so it is not actually a common factor at all, and 18 is one of the original numbers, not a factor shared with 27.
exitTicket.hint: Think through the problem step by step.
choiceFeedback: 3 divides both, but is there a LARGER shared factor of 18 and 27?
Does 6 divide 27 evenly? Recheck your common factors.
18 doesn't divide 27 — the GCF must divide BOTH numbers.
hints: The GCF must divide BOTH 18 and 27 evenly — and it has to be the GREATEST number that does, not just any shared factor.
List every factor of 18, then every factor of 27, and compare the two lists before you pick.
Write 18's six factors (from 1 up to 18) and 27's four factors. Circle the shared ones and choose the largest circle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 17 has exactly two factors: 1 and 17. 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7, and 9 = 3 × 3, so they are all composite.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 18?
questions.explanation: 18 = 2 × 9 = 2 × 3 × 3. Both 2 and 3 are prime, so 2 × 3 × 3 is the prime factorization.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 30?
questions.explanation: 30 = 2 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 5. All three factors (2, 3, 5) are prime, so 2 × 3 × 5 is the prime factorization.
